title: What does EU GMP Chapter 2 require for pharmaceutical personnel training?
description: What EU GMP Guide Part I Chapter 2 requires for personnel training, key roles and records, plus Chapter 4 and Annex 11 revision status, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: Chapter 2 (Personnel) of the EU Guidelines for Good Manufacturing Practice, Part I, requires medicine manufacturers to train everyone whose work takes them into production, storage or quality control areas, or whose activities could affect product quality. Training must cover GMP and the quality management system, be given at recruitment and on a continuing basis, follow programs approved by the head of Production or Quality Control, be periodically assessed for effectiveness, and be recorded.
keyTakeaways: The binding duty is in Commission Directive (EU) 2017/1572, Article 7(4): personnel receive initial and ongoing training whose effectiveness is verified. Chapter 2 of EudraLex Volume 4 explains how inspectors expect that to be done.
Chapter 2 has been in operation since 16 February 2014. It applies to technical, maintenance and cleaning staff, not only operators and analysts.
Training programs must be approved by the head of Production or the head of Quality Control, and the practical effectiveness of continuing training must be periodically assessed.
Staff in clean areas or areas handling highly active, toxic, infectious or sensitizing materials need specific training; consultants need documented qualifications.

As at November 2026, Chapter 4 (Documentation) and Annex 11 (Computerised Systems) remain the January 2011 versions. Revised drafts and a new Annex 22 on AI went to public consultation from 7 July to 7 October 2025 and have not yet been adopted.
jurisdiction: European Union (EU Member States; the EEA applies the same guidelines)
regulator: European Commission (EudraLex Volume 4 guidelines), with GMP inspections carried out by the national competent authorities of the Member States
appliesTo: Holders of a manufacturing authorization for human or veterinary medicinal products, including importers
All personnel whose duties take them into production, storage or quality control areas, including technical, maintenance and cleaning staff
Key personnel: head of Production, head of Quality Control, head of Quality Assurance or Quality Unit where appointed, and the Qualified Person (QP)

sections.heading: Where does the EU GMP training duty come from?

blocks.text: The legal duty sits in Commission Directive (EU) 2017/1572, and Chapter 2 of the EU GMP Guide explains how to meet it. [Article 7 of Directive (EU) 2017/1572](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32017L1572) requires a sufficient number of competent and appropriately qualified personnel at each manufacturing or import site, and states in paragraph 4:

blocks.title: Directive (EU) 2017/1572, Article 7(4)
blocks.text: "The personnel shall receive initial and ongoing training, the effectiveness of which shall be verified, covering in particular the theory and application of the concept of quality assurance and good manufacturing practice."

The detailed guidance is published by the European Commission in EudraLex Volume 4, the EU Guidelines for Good Manufacturing Practice for Medicinal Products for Human and Veterinary Use. [Part I, Chapter 2: Personnel](https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/11f4f8e6-a6e9-4897-afe3-f21e1dc56cb8_en?filename=2014-03_chapter_2.pdf) was revised to integrate the pharmaceutical quality system concepts of ICH Q10 and to add a section on consultants, with a deadline for coming into operation of 16 February 2014. Inspectors from Member State competent authorities assess compliance during GMP inspections. Everything below reflects the Chapter 2 text and EudraLex listings as at November 2026.

Chapter 2 is the EU counterpart of the US drug CGMP training rule covered in [FDA GMP personnel training requirements](/regulations/fda-gmp-personnel-training-requirements). Sites that manufacture for both markets usually run one training system, but the EU text puts more weight on management responsibility, approval of training programs, and verifying effectiveness.

sections.heading: Who must receive GMP training under Chapter 2?

blocks.text: Everyone whose work could affect product quality must be trained, not just production operators. Paragraph 2.10 says the manufacturer should provide training for "all the personnel whose duties take them into production and storage areas or into control laboratories (including the technical, maintenance and cleaning personnel), and for other personnel whose activities could affect the quality of the product."

In practice that scope reaches warehouse staff, engineers and contractors who maintain equipment, cleaning crews, and office functions such as artwork, supplier qualification or IT support for GMP systems. Paragraph 2.13 adds that visitors or untrained personnel should preferably not enter production and quality control areas; where that is unavoidable, they should be briefed in advance on personal hygiene and protective clothing and be closely supervised.

Paragraph 2.23 extends the expectation to consultants. They should have adequate education, training and experience to advise on the subject they are retained for, and records should state their name, address, qualifications and the type of service provided.

sections.heading: What must GMP training cover and when?

blocks.text: Chapter 2 requires three layers: basic GMP and quality system training, role-specific training for new starters, and continuing training whose effectiveness is checked. Paragraph 2.11 sets this out:

blocks.title: EU GMP Guide Part I, paragraph 2.11
blocks.text: "Besides the basic training on the theory and practice of the quality management system and Good Manufacturing Practice, newly recruited personnel should receive training appropriate to the duties assigned to them. Continuing training should also be given, and its practical effectiveness should be periodically assessed. Training programmes should be available, approved by either the head of Production or the head of Quality Control, as appropriate. Training records should be kept."

items: **Contamination hazard areas (2.12):** personnel working in clean areas or where highly active, toxic, infectious or sensitizing materials are handled should be given specific training. Sterile manufacturing adds further requirements, covered in [EU GMP Annex 1 sterile manufacturing training](/regulations/eu-gmp-annex-1-sterile-manufacturing-training).
**Quality system (2.14):** the pharmaceutical quality system and measures that improve its understanding and implementation should be fully discussed during training sessions.

**Hygiene (2.15 to 2.21):** detailed hygiene programs covering health, hygiene practices and clothing should be promoted by management and widely discussed during training. Personnel should be instructed to use hand-washing facilities, and all personnel should receive a medical examination on recruitment.

**No fixed frequency:** Chapter 2 does not set an annual cycle. It requires continuing training adapted to need and a periodic assessment of its practical effectiveness, so each site must define and justify its own intervals.

blocks.text: Because no interval is prescribed, inspectors look for a documented rationale. A risk-based method is described in [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

sections.heading: Who is accountable for GMP training?

blocks.text: Senior management is ultimately accountable, and the heads of Production and Quality Control are named as responsible for their departments' training. Paragraph 2.1 requires senior management to provide adequate resources, including human resources, to implement and maintain the quality management system, and paragraph 2.4 gives senior management ultimate responsibility for an effective quality management system with defined, communicated roles.

Paragraphs 2.7(vi) and 2.8(vii) make the head of Production and the head of Quality Control each responsible for ensuring "that the required initial and continuing training of his department personnel is carried out and adapted according to need." Paragraph 2.9 lists training among the shared responsibilities of the heads of Production, Quality Control and, where one exists, Quality Assurance or the Quality Unit. Paragraph 2.3 requires people in responsible positions to have written job descriptions, and deputies must be of a satisfactory qualification level.

The Qualified Person has separate statutory qualification requirements under Article 49 of Directive 2001/83/EC, referenced in paragraph 2.6, and QP duties can be delegated only to another QP. Those requirements are outside the scope of this page.

sections.heading: Are the documentation and computerized system rules for training records changing?

blocks.text: Yes, but not yet. As at November 2026, the [EudraLex Volume 4 page](https://health.ec.europa.eu/medicinal-products/eudralex/eudralex-volume-4_en) still lists Chapter 4 (Documentation) dated January 2011 and Annex 11 (Computerised Systems) as the January 2011 revision. These govern how training records are created, controlled and kept when they are on paper or in an electronic system.

blocks.title: In consultation: not in force as at November 2026
blocks.text: The European Commission ran a [stakeholder consultation on revised Chapter 4, revised Annex 11 and a new Annex 22 on artificial intelligence](https://health.ec.europa.eu/consultations/stakeholders-consultation-eudralex-volume-4-good-manufacturing-practice-guidelines-chapter-4-annex_en) from 7 July 2025 to 7 October 2025. The drafts were prepared by the EMA GMDP Inspectors Working Group with PIC/S. The draft Annex 11 includes a "Personnel and Training" section requiring system-specific training matched to each person's responsibilities and access privileges, and recurrent security awareness training whose effectiveness is evaluated, for example by simulated tests. A separate consultation on Chapter 1 closed on 3 December 2025.

The current Annex 11 already expects close cooperation between process owners, system owners, Qualified Persons and IT, and states that all personnel should have appropriate qualifications, level of access and defined responsibilities. Sites that keep training records in a learning management system should treat that system as a GMP computerized system now, and plan for the draft's explicit training and data integrity expectations once a final text is published.

sections.heading: What training records should be ready for a GMP inspection?

blocks.text: Inspectors expect records that show who was trained, on which approved program and procedure version, when, and how effectiveness was checked. Paragraph 2.11 requires training records to be kept; Chapter 4 governs their control and retention.

items: The organization chart required by paragraph 2.2 and job descriptions for people in responsible positions (2.3).
Approved training programs, with the approver (head of Production or head of Quality Control) and version history.
Individual training records linked to the SOP versions in force at the time.
Evidence of effectiveness assessment for continuing training, not only attendance.
Specific training records for clean area and hazardous material staff, cross-referenced to access rights.
Management review records showing training is considered when the quality system is reviewed (2.4).

blocks.text: For how to assemble this evidence, see [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) and [how to evidence training effectiveness to a regulator](/guides/how-to-evidence-training-effectiveness-to-a-regulator).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each Chapter 2 paragraph to the site's own SOPs, the roles that perform them, and the assessment points used to verify effectiveness. When a procedure changes, the affected roles can be identified from those links and assigned retraining against the new version. See how this applies to [healthcare and life sciences organizations](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Does EU GMP require annual GMP refresher training?
faqs.a: No fixed frequency is set. Chapter 2 requires continuing training and a periodic assessment of its practical effectiveness, and Directive (EU) 2017/1572 requires ongoing training whose effectiveness is verified. Many sites choose an annual GMP refresher, but the interval should be justified by risk and by the evidence from effectiveness checks.

faqs.q: Who must approve GMP training programs in the EU?
faqs.a: Paragraph 2.11 says training programs should be approved by either the head of Production or the head of Quality Control, as appropriate. Where a site has a separate head of Quality Assurance or Quality Unit, training is listed in paragraph 2.9 as a shared responsibility, so the approval route should be defined in the site's procedures.

faqs.q: Do cleaning and maintenance contractors need GMP training?
faqs.a: Yes, if their duties take them into production, storage or quality control areas. Paragraph 2.10 names technical, maintenance and cleaning personnel explicitly. Contractors who only enter occasionally can be handled as visitors under paragraph 2.13, with advance hygiene and clothing information and close supervision.

faqs.q: Does Chapter 2 apply to active substance manufacturers?
faqs.a: Active substance manufacturing follows Part II of the EU GMP Guide (Basic requirements for active substances used as starting materials), which has its own personnel section. Chapter 2 is part of Part I, which covers finished medicinal products for human and veterinary use.
